Liberation is totally independent. No state, experience or even practice is required for its realisation. Yet the separate self believes it needs to be liberated, and this is indeed apt - the delusion of separation is the context in which liberation applies, it is that which one is liberated from. But there is no separation, so the idea of liberation itself is delusional. As long as the false belief in the separate self exists there is no liberation, and yet in truth liberation is there eternally without fail. The need for liberation, and the impossibility of its being attained, are essential traits of the inessential self. Simply forget the assumption of your self, and liberation is revealed, though to call it liberation is to maintain the idea of the separate self as having some reality or relevance. Without such a notion there simply is what is.
